% Shared normative equations.
\section{Model, measurement, and conditional estimators}\label{sec:equations}

\subsection{Invariant zero-background source model}\label{sec:model}

For physical tangent coordinate $\uvec_q$, the only base model family is
\begin{equation}
g_q(A,\boldsymbol{\mu},\Sigmashape)
=A\exp\!\left[-\tfrac12(\uvec_q-\boldsymbol{\mu})^{\mathsf T}
\Sigmashape^{-1}(\uvec_q-\boldsymbol{\mu})\right],
\label{eq:gaussian}
\end{equation}
where $\Sigmashape$ is symmetric positive definite. The invariant principal
extents are strictly positive and ordered major not less than minor. The
source model has no constant, gradient, local baseline, or other nuisance
term. Its six roles are amplitude, two centroid coordinates, two
principal-width roles, and orientation.

The exact numerical parameter ordering, published width convention, angle
origin, positive direction, gauge/period canonicalization, amplitude domain,
parameter bounds, active-bound interpretation, and source-profile convention
remain unavailable until \CompatMethod{} is owner-approved. At exact
circularity, orientation is \texttt{undefined\_by\_model\_symmetry}; a finite
placeholder is not a measurement. Exchanging principal axes with the
corresponding angle transformation leaves Equation~\ref{eq:gaussian}
invariant.

\subsection{Coordinate transform and signed displacement}\label{sec:displacement}

For parent coordinate $p_q$, the exact AST boundary supplies
\begin{equation}
\uvec_q=T(p_q;\,\text{coordinate state}).
\label{eq:transform}
\end{equation}
The model shall use the physical tangent metric, not storage-pixel distance,
unless the boundary proves their equivalence over admitted support. The
ordered basis vectors, handedness, positive directions, angular unit, time and
state, Jacobian where relevant, support, uncertainty, lifecycle, provenance,
and failure behavior are all bound facts. Axis labels, memory order, display
orientation, and FITS array order are not sign authority.

The measurement is
\begin{equation}
\DeltaPoint=\muhat-\muexp,
\qquad [\DeltaPoint]=\mathrm{arcsec},
\label{eq:displacement}
\end{equation}
in that exact basis. If the tangent-coordinate origin equals the expected
position, $\muexp=(0,0)$ and $\DeltaPoint=\muhat$. The search center affects
search and initialization only and never defines the zero point. POINT owns
the sign in Equation~\ref{eq:displacement}; correction sign and composition
are downstream.

\subsection{Conditional numerical fit}\label{sec:conditional-fit}

The most that can be stated before method recovery is
\begin{equation}
\thetahat=
\operatorname{Resolve}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\in\Theta_{\mathrm{effective}}}
D\!\left(m,g_{\boldsymbol{\theta}};W_{\mathrm{fit}}\right).
\label{eq:conditional-fit}
\end{equation}
The admitted rows, scalar objective or likelihood $D$, weight meaning and
normalization, constraints, comparison of multiple solutions, convergence,
retry, and solution rule are not supplied. Equation~\ref{eq:conditional-fit}
shall not be instantiated by guessing least squares, inverse variance,
reliability weighting, or covariance weighting. Fit weights, parent
stochastic covariance, inverse covariance, the formal-error model, and parent
uncertainty are distinct roles.

The preserved mature procedure has configurable expected-center/central
search, weighted-peak initialization, global fallback, bounded fit domain,
and amplitude/width/angle constraints. Request, effective configuration,
resolved plan, application attempt, and realized fit remain distinct. A
sentinel shall resolve to a named effective state, and every fallback,
restart, retry, branch, bound, and termination shall be reported. Exact rules
belong to \CompatMethod{}.

\subsection{Association is not optimization}\label{sec:association}

Expected position, requested search center, effective search center, selected
seed, fitted centroid, and source association are distinct. Every central,
global-fallback, restart, retry, or other authorized branch yields a candidate
seed, never source identity. Source-attributed displacement and amplitude
require \path{POINT-SOURCE-ASSOCIATION-STATE=established} under one
branch-independent method and declared association domain. A central or
global peak, finite fit, small displacement, large amplitude, dynamic range,
or formal standardization cannot establish association. The numerical
\path{POINT-FIT-AMPLITUDE-COMPONENT} may survive unavailable or failed
association, but only
\path{POINT-SOURCE-ASSOCIATED-AMPLITUDE-DIAGNOSTIC} is attributable to the
intended source.

\subsection{Residual and deterministic mismatch}\label{sec:residual}

The scientific decomposition is
\begin{equation}
m=g(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{\mathrm{true}})+b+n,
\label{eq:residual}
\end{equation}
where $b$ is any deterministic parent component not represented by the
zero-background model and $n$ is stochastic variation. POINT neither fits nor
silently removes $b$. It can bias every fit role; a finite fit does not turn
it into noise. Once fitting is authorized, the fitted model and residual
shall be published or reconstructible with objective, support, row count,
rank, convergence, active constraints, branch state, residual diagnostics,
and parent additive-reference/null state.

\subsection{Conditional diagnostic identities}\label{sec:diagnostics}

Only two derived product identities are admitted. The role is
\begin{center}
\path{POINT-DYNAMIC-RANGE-DIAGNOSTIC/}\\
\path{FITTED-AMPLITUDE-OVER-FULL-MAP-RMS@1}.
\end{center}
Its conditional formula is
\begin{align}
D_{\mathrm{RMS}}&=\widehat A/\mathrm{RMS}_{\mathrm{full}}.
\label{eq:dynamic-range}
\end{align}
The role \path{POINT-FORMAL-AMPLITUDE-STANDARDIZATION@1} has the conditional
formula
\begin{equation}
Z_A=\widehat A/\sigma_A.
\label{eq:formal-standardization}
\end{equation}
Equation~\ref{eq:dynamic-range} is descriptive dynamic range only and is
unavailable until \RMSMethod{} binds the parent/generation, population,
centering, weighting, source-region treatment, support/edge, non-finite and
zero-denominator rules, units, lifecycle, provenance, and parent relation. It
requires the exact selected fit-amplitude role, a compatible parent and
generation, a finite positive denominator, and the association state required
by the declared diagnostic claim. \texttt{sig2noise} may be an exact legacy
alias only after \RMSMethod{} explicitly proves mathematical identity with
this signed ratio and approves that alias.
\texttt{peak\_over\_full\_map\_rms} is not admitted without a separate
compatibility-method finding.

Equations~\ref{eq:dynamic-range} and \ref{eq:formal-standardization} retain
the sign of the approved fitted amplitude; the dynamic-range diagnostic is
therefore not universally nonnegative. Equation~\ref{eq:formal-standardization}
is the canonical signed
\path{POINT-FORMAL-AMPLITUDE-STANDARDIZATION@1}. It is unavailable until
\FormalMethod{} is approved and $\sigma_A$ is positive and finite. It requires
the exact selected fit-amplitude role and its approved formal amplitude error.
An absolute-magnitude quantity would instead have the distinct identity
\path{POINT-FORMAL-AMPLITUDE-MAGNITUDE-STANDARDIZATION@1} and formula
$|\widehat A|/\sigma_A$; it is not admitted unless separately requested and
authorized.
\texttt{fit\_sig2noise} may be an exact legacy alias only after \FormalMethod{}
proves mathematical identity with the signed canonical quantity and explicitly
approves that alias. Neither ratio is statistical
significance, detection probability, false-alarm statistic, completeness, or
purity. A zero or non-finite denominator produces the future method's typed
unavailable or failed state, never an infinite claim.

Each derived role has its own request, parent, method, producer lifecycle,
availability, support, unit-one state, cause, provenance, and claim ceiling.
Neither role is required for fit-result completion. Any diagnostic described
as applying to the intended source additionally requires
\path{POINT-SOURCE-ASSOCIATION-STATE=established}; no ratio promotes an
unassociated amplitude component into a source-associated role.

\subsection{Conditional response objects}\label{sec:response-equations}

For one frozen branch $b$, resolved state $g$, and perturbation coordinate
$m$, the fixed-branch parameter response, when differentiable or under another
exact authorized local perturbation rule, is
\begin{equation}
R^{\mathrm{fixed}}_{\theta,m}
=\left.\frac{\partial\thetahat}{\partial m}\right|_{b,g,\,
\mathrm{support},\,W_{\mathrm{fit}},\,\mathrm{constraints}} ,
\label{eq:fixed-response}
\end{equation}
and the displacement response is
\begin{equation}
R^{\mathrm{fixed}}_{\Delta,m}=P_{\mu}R^{\mathrm{fixed}}_{\theta,m}.
\label{eq:fixed-displacement-response}
\end{equation}

For perturbation direction $\delta m$, the POINT full-procedure response with
the parent product held fixed is
\begin{equation}
R^{\mathrm{POINT\mbox{-}FP}\mid\mathrm{parent\mbox{-}fixed}}_{\theta,m}
[\delta m]
=\lim_{\epsilon\rightarrow0}
\frac{\widehat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{\mathcal P}
(m+\epsilon\,\delta m)-
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{\mathcal P}(m)}{\epsilon},
\label{eq:full-procedure-response}
\end{equation}
or one separately authorized finite-difference equivalent. Both invocations
of $\mathcal{P}$ rerun central search, fallback, restarts and retries, support
resolution, applicable weight/state resolution, constraint activation,
optimization, and association, but do not rerun the upstream parent producer.
The numerator subtracts comparable numerical parameter outputs, never
lifecycle, decision, or record objects.

Comparability requires the same intended source, compatible association,
identical parameter roles, compatible gauge and canonical ordering, compatible
units and basis, availability of the target components, and a valid relation
between the two perturbation domains. If those conditions do not hold, the
response is unavailable or the result is a separately typed discontinuity or
state transition; it is not silently represented as a derivative. Every
response record binds the baseline and perturbed products and states,
perturbation source, domain, direction, unit, and $\epsilon$, finite or analytic
convention, branch changes, gauge comparison, component availability, exact
cause, and provenance.

A source-domain fixed differential response may be composed only with a
compatible exact fixed parent response:
\begin{equation}
R^{\mathrm{fixed}}_{\theta,\mathrm{source}}
=R^{\mathrm{fixed}}_{\theta,m}
 R^{\mathrm{fixed}}_{m,\mathrm{source}}.
\label{eq:source-response}
\end{equation}
The POINT-full-procedure/parent-fixed response above and a whole-chain
full-procedure response
$R^{\mathrm{chain\mbox{-}FP}}_{\theta,\mathrm{source}}$ are also distinct.
The latter exists only under authority to rerun the complete upstream parent
production and POINT procedure together. Fixed parent composition,
POINT-full-procedure with a fixed parent, and whole-chain full-procedure never
alias one another. A finite-difference response shall not be multiplied as a
Jacobian unless an exact composition theorem for those defined procedures and
domains has been authorized.

Parent response, each of these POINT or whole-chain response types, and
empirical observational bias/accuracy are distinct products. Under one declared
empirical population and procedure, observational displacement bias may be
defined as
\begin{equation}
b_{\Delta}=\mathbb{E}\!\left[
\widehat{\Delta}-\Delta_{\mathrm{true}}
\mid \text{population and procedure}\right].
\label{eq:observational-bias}
\end{equation}
No unavailable response or bias is numerically zero.

\subsection{Conditional displacement covariance}\label{sec:displacement-covariance}

When fitted-centroid and expected-position covariance objects and both cross
covariances are available in one common tangent basis,
\begin{equation}
C_{\Delta}=C_{\muhat}+C_{\muexp}
-C_{\muhat,\muexp}-C_{\muexp,\muhat}.
\label{eq:displacement-covariance}
\end{equation}
Neither cross term is zero without explicit independence authority. If a
coordinate transformation is required, its Jacobian and the complete joint
covariance shall be bound before transformation. If any required covariance
or cross-covariance is unavailable, the combined displacement covariance is
unavailable while available component uncertainties remain visible.
